test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true about the mass of an object?

options.text: It stays the same no matter where the object is.
It changes from place to place.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It stays the same no matter where the object is**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental property of matter that represents the total amount of **matter** or **atoms** contained within an object.
 
• Statement 1: It depends on gravity. This statement is **incorrect**. **Mass** is independent of **gravitational pull**. It is **weight** that depends on the **acceleration due to gravity** (**g**).
 
• Statement 2: It stays the same no matter where the object is. This statement is **correct** because **mass** is an **intrinsic property**. Whether the object is on **Earth**, the **Moon**, or in **outer space**, the quantity of matter it contains does not change. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 3: It increases at pole. This statement is **incorrect**. While the **weight** of an object increases at the **Earth's poles** because the **Earth** is not a perfect sphere and the **gravitational force** is stronger there, the **mass** remains **constant**.
 
• Statement 4: It changes from place to place. This statement is **incorrect**. This is a characteristic of **weight**, which varies depending on the **altitude**, **latitude**, or the **celestial body** the object is placed upon.
 
• **Mass** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it only has **magnitude** and no **direction**. It can never be **zero** for a physical object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Measurement Units**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• Other common units include **grams (g)**, **milligrams (mg)**, and **tonnes (1,000 kg)**.
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Weight**:
 
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted by **gravity** on an object. It is calculated using the formula **W = m × g**, where **m** is **mass** and **g** is **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²** on **Earth**).
 
• Since **g** varies at different locations, **weight** changes, but **mass** (**m**) remains the same.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**:
 
 
• **Mass** is often described as a measure of **inertia**. **Inertia** is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its **state of motion**.
 
• An object with a larger **mass** has greater **inertia**, making it harder to start moving, stop, or change its **direction**.
 
 
 
• **Measuring Instruments**:
 
 
• **Mass** is typically measured using a **beam balance** or a **physical balance**, which compares an unknown mass against **standard masses**.
 
• **Weight** is measured using a **spring balance**, which measures the **force** of gravity pulling on the object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation of Mass**: In **classical physics** and **chemical reactions**, the **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that **mass** can neither be created nor destroyed; it only changes forms.
 
• **Difference on the Moon**: The **gravity** on the **Moon** is only **1/6th** of that on **Earth**. If an object has a **mass** of **60 kg**, it will still have a **mass** of **60 kg** on the **Moon**, but its **weight** will drop from **588 N** (on Earth) to approximately **98 N**.
 
• **Atomic Mass**: On a microscopic scale, the **mass** of an atom is measured in **Atomic Mass Units (amu)**, defined as **1/12th** of the **mass** of a **carbon-12 atom**.
 
• **Relativistic Mass**: According to **Einstein's Theory of Relativity**, as an object approaches the **speed of light**, its **relativistic mass** increases, though its **rest mass** remains unchanged.
</ul
